dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Muskets aren't like crayon drawings – you can't just add something simply because you felt like it! Incremental, sensible upgrades are the only way forward... Some people are already slacking off on maintenance. The last thing we need is to throw radical modifications into the mix.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We modifying muskets here?

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Yes. As you can see, I'm a gunsmith with 8th Company. My job is to provide technical support to the marksmen in each squad.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: In recent years, we've started to equip muskets on a small scale.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: The muskets we're using, which are produced for us by Support Company's workshop, incorporate advanced technology from both Snezhnaya and Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: In terms of overall performance, they're on par with the models used by the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol and the Oprichniki. For your run-of-the-mill monsters, they're more than enough.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: However, there are always knights who demand instant and overwhelming firepower. They keep hounding us to make major modifications to our tried-and-tested models.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: For example... They talk about switching from tubular magazines to box magazines. That way, you don't have to insert rounds one by one. Instead, you can clip in a whole box of rounds and off you go.

choices.text: Wouldn't that make firing more efficient?

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: That is correct, yes. To be clear, I am all for improving our firearms.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: But modifications like this are easier said than done, as they call for a whole suite of changes. For example, you'd also need to standardize the size and manufacturing of the metal clips, move to mass production, and implement proper packaging too.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: It's not just about a simple design tweak — Support Company will have to handle all that, too. They can badger me all they want, but I'm just a gunsmith!

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: Loading mods aside, there's even an article from Snezhnaya which proposes the addition of a cam slot to the locking mechanism, linked to the bolt by a connecting rod, and using recoil to eject the spent casing...

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: And then a spring built into the stock (or mounted externally) drives the bolt forward, automatically chambers the next round, and the musket continues firing...

choices.text: Wow, that sounds like quite the beast.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: Ahem, I'd certainly love to have a weapon that can fire continuously in rapid succession too... especially those cutting-edge Fatui armaments they have in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: But since those rotary-barrel weapons aren't on the market yet at this time, we'll have to develop our own rapid-fire mechanisms...

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: In fact, I did work with Herstal to create three prototypes and put them to the test in continuous-fire experiments.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: With the first prototype, we were unable to resolve the bolt's rotational unlocking issue. It kept jamming, so we had to modify the op rod.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: The second prototype's op rod shattered after we fired 97 rounds on it, and the rod fragments wrecked Herstal's antique teacup...

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: In the third case, we found severe wear and tear in the prototype's chamber after firing some 240 rounds with it. The locking mechanism had failed, the stock was cracked open, and the spring was a goner too.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: We also faced several other thorny issues, like the weapon venting hot air directly into the firer's face, making it impossible to see.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: Eventually, I concluded that rapid continuous fire just isn't possible without a fundamental redesign of the weapon's basic structure.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: A side-linked bolt system simply isn't the answer, since the operating mechanism has to be aligned with the barrel axis to prevent uneven points of stress.

response.speaker: Koch
response.text: ...I do wonder if we could use a combination of components like rollers and locking recesses to delay bolt unlocking. That might just mitigate the chamber pressure issue just enough...

choices.text: You have to admit, rapid continuous fire does sound really powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's getting lazy with their maintenance? Go straighten him out!

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: It's Gunther. He keeps dumping his weapon cleaning on us gunsmiths because "he's the perennial champ of the company's shoots."

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Argh... Muskets are works of art, for goodness' sake! If I were a better shot than him, I'd make him bow his head and apologize to those muskets properly!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think that's the only thing that's bothering you...

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Huh. Are you a mind reader or something?

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: I did run into a bit of trouble... I ordered a batch of metal materials that was to be transported here overland...

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: But the merchants transporting the materials were taken by some unknown monsters in the wilderness, and no one knows where the shipment is now.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'd paid for this order out of my own pocket as I wanted to try making some new parts, so I can't possibly ask the other knights to go through the trouble of tracking it down for me.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: I guess I'll just have to see if I can take some time off to go look for it myself...

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: No way! What a stroke of luck!

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: These are the materials I'd bought with money out of my own pocket to develop new parts!

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: I had the merchants transport the shipment overland, but the cargo was taken by some unknown monsters in the wilderness... No one knew where it was.

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: It's been giving me a massive headache, so much so that I even thought about taking a few days off to look for the shipment myself. But now the problem's all solved!

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! Thank you so very much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have my support — take your time to figure things out!

dialogues.speaker: Koch
dialogues.text: Um, my apologies! I guess I got a little carried away with my complaining.
